newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Africans appeal for change in high-risk image.
newsitem.headline: Africans appeal for change in high-risk image.

text.p: Development ministers from the world's poorest continent on Friday urged leaders to change the negative image of Africa as a high-risk environment in order to attract foreign investment and bolster growth.

"Africa needs trade and investment as essential components in any credible strategies to accelerate development and sustain high rates of economic growth," the ministers for economic or social development said in statement in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

"We are convinced that poverty, which constitutes the most serious problem facing African society today, can be reduced and eventually eradicated by sustained high rates of economic growth which require a sustained high rate of investment and production," they said after a five-day conference.
The conference in the Ethiopian capital was called by the U.N. Economic Commission for Africa, which is raising its profile as a debate forum for Africa's economic development.

The ministers said they were convinced that Africa needed foreign investment to speed up economic growth. To attract foreign capital transfers and expand trade with the rest of the world, the ministers said a change of image was paramount.
They wanted a change in the negative perception of Africa as a high-risk place and improved information flow on development.
They said improving Africa's image was in great part in the hands of African political leaders.

They wanted to see modernisation, expansion and diversifying of production, lower costs of establishing and doing business in Africa, strengthening international competitiveness, genuine regional economic integration and effective participation in the multinational trading system, the statement said.
The ministers welcomed a new debt reduction initiative for the highly indebted poor countries as a first step in the right direction. Uganda is expected to be first to benefit.
They appealed to creditors to seek more ways of reducing Africa's external debt, which stands at around $340 billion, saying debt servicing siphoned away valuable resources.
The statement deplored the marginalisation of Africa at a time when significant positive developments were taking place.

The ministers said they were concerned about the declining official development assistance to Africa despite strict economic restructuring efforts across the continent and the continuing need for development resources.
